chunks: Ali narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

If a woman kills a man, she is killed for him. And if a man kills a woman, then if they want retaliation, they pay the excess of the man’s blood money and then retaliate against him for her; and if they do not do that, they accept the blood money—the woman’s blood money in full. And the blood money of a woman is half the blood money of a man.

key_terms.الْقَوَدَ: legal retaliation, meaning qisas for intentional killing
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman, referring here to the female victim or perpetrator in homicide rulings
key_terms.دِيَةِ: blood money, the prescribed financial compensation for homicide
key_terms.رَجُلًا: a man, referring to the male victim in the ruling
key_terms.فَضْلَ دِيَةِ الرَّجُلِ: the difference or excess amount of the man’s blood money that must be paid
key_terms.نِصْفُ: half, indicating the proportional legal amount of diyah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on qisas and diyah when a man kills a woman or a woman kills a man in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling on retaliation and blood money in cases of homicide between a man and a woman. It explains when qisas is applied and clarifies that the diyah of a woman is half the diyah of a man in this legal context.
